audits.mathematicalReason: Write the six consecutive numbers as n through n+5. Since 11 and 15 occur, n must be 10 or 11. Their total is 6n+15, so the common opposite-face sum is 2n+5. If n=10, that sum is 25, forcing 11 and 14 onto opposite faces, contrary to the diagram. If n=11, the opposite pairs can be (11,16), (14,13), and (15,12), consistent with the three visible adjacent faces. Thus the total is 81. Recognizing adjacent versus opposite cube faces and finding complementary addends support the assessed mapping; listing consecutive numbers supports cnm_p060.

These coefficients can alternatively be obtained by recursively counting downward supporting paths, starting with weight 1 at the top. If a larger label x occupies a larger coefficient a while a smaller label y occupies b<a, swapping them decreases the total by (a-b)(x-y). Hence a minimum assigns 1 to coefficient 6, labels 2 through 7 to the six coefficient-3 positions, and 8 through 10 to the vertices. This attains 6+3(2+3+4+5+6+7)+8+9+10=114. The exchange bound and attaining assignment satisfy the extremal scope. The two coefficient-finding routes are valid alternatives, not joint requirements.
